description: TU Delft provides raw, processed and result data for combining cycling with public transport to improve job accessibility in Amsterdam. Raw inputs describe road-segment cycling speeds, transit schedules, sociodemographics and streets. Processed products include walking and cycling travel times and study boundaries. Result fields include shortest paths, perceived travel time, job accessibility, utility changes and candidate cycle lanes and bicycle parking. Coverage: No complete measurement interval or evaluation extent is stated in the reviewed source. Access: public native metadata describes the release and its formats. Licence: CC-BY-4.0. Cost and current distribution access remain unknown. Caveats: This dataset is paired with a distinct native code release. It includes derived results and does not establish current infrastructure or current transit schedules. Files, demographic representativeness and accessibility calculations were not independently examined. The paired network model uses these inputs for cycling-infrastructure planning.
